children: Micron (MU) guides fiscal Q1 revenue ~$61.5B ±$1.5B, diluted EPS ~ $38.15 ±$1.00, and gross margin ~86.25%.
Micron (MU) inked 26 long-term supply deals worth $32B, up from $22B a year earlier. Contracts extend into 2031, covering 35%+ of expected revenue through 2030; RPOs ~ $150B.
Micron (MU) says memory demand will stay tight into fiscal 2027–2028 and plans about $25 billion in capex for H1 FY2027, including roughly $11.5 billion in Q1.
Micron (MU) saw broad growth from AI demand and customer deals, plans factory expansions and tech investments, and expects FY2027 record results as supply stays tight and margins rise.
Micron (MU) may start larger buybacks from Dec. 9, limited by CHIPS Act rules. It has $2.2 billion left under its current repurchase authorization.
Micron (MU) expects gross margin to slip to 86.3% from 87.0% this quarter, citing higher incentive pay and manufacturing wage costs booked through inventory; company calls it a margin low point.
Micron (MU) traders watch DRAM pricing and the memory cycle into 2027; DRAM contract-price guidance will drive stock moves due to its large impact on margins in Micron’s high fixed‑cost model.
Netlist asked the U.S. ITC to block imports of certain Micron chips used in AI systems by Nvidia, Google and Broadcom; the ITC case could limit those Micron products’ U.S. imports.
Micron (MU) faces pressure as Chinese rival CXMT plans to raise wafer starts to ~20,000/month by year‑end, adding supply that could affect Micron's pricing and margins amid weak PC and phone demand.
Micron (MU) is sampling 512GB DDR5 RDIMMs at high speeds, completed customer qualifications for faster server RDIMMs, and is shipping PCIe Gen5 and Gen6 SSDs for KV-cache applications.
